headline: Gate C (partial, QUALIFIED — reduced retention/access coupling, NOT MD-resolved PMF): an endogenous membrane PAYS FOR ITSELF ON PERSISTENCE, not throughput. On the Gate-B pore-concentrated A1 (sustained, NON-autocatalytic) network, at Jordan-2019 vent-calibrated retention 0.905 / access 0.997 (grounded, not tuned), the membrane retains 2.9x the standing metabolite pool vs the matched no-membrane ablation (persistence_pays=True); net fixation FLUX is 0.63x (throughput_pays=False). The throughput-null is the PHYSICALLY EXPECTED result, not a shortcoming: a membrane acts on retention (lowers washout -> raises the standing pool), and at steady state with fixed feed the fixation RATE is feed-limited, so persistence rises while throughput stays flat/down. The scientific takeaway: compartmentalization buys retention/concentration, not faster chemistry. The persistence benefit is WINDOWED: it holds for access >= ~0.45 and inverts below (a too-tight membrane starves the network faster than retention helps, so the retained pool falls below the open system); the vent-calibrated access 0.997 sits comfortably inside. Four qualifications on the positive: persistence-only (throughput feed-limited), windowed, reduced coupling (not MD-PMF), and PARTIAL Gate C (full = study 32 First Self-Maintaining Protocell + viva-md-membrane MD-resolved coupling).
